summary: Bluff Mountain tower, Rockbridge County VA: build year disputed (1917 or 1930); removed early 2000s over Punchbowl Shelter concerns; footings or foundation remain; hike access.

facts.design: Planned forty-foot steel tower with a 14 x 14 foot cabin, per a September 3, 1932 newspaper item; not confirmed as built
facts.status_note: Removed in the early 2000s per the register; the Lexington guide says a foundation and steps remain, the Appalachian Trail history site says only footings remain

access.note: Summit reached on foot along the Appalachian Trail (Lexington visitor guide)

visit.trail_note: No tower remains to climb. The Lexington guide describes the hike to the summit and a side trail to Punchbowl Shelter about four-tenths of a mile in.

events.note: Appalachian Trail history site says the U.S. Forest Service built a tower around 1917; conflicts with the register's 1930

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register gives 1930. The Appalachian Trail history site says the Forest Service built a tower around 1917. A News Leader item dated September 3, 1932, quoted on the Forest Lookouts page, announces a tower that would be constructed; the Trail history site paraphrases a 1932 newspaper announcement. A 1933 survey describes the fire tower as already on the summit. The story gives the sources' dates without choosing one.
The Lexington guide says the foundation and steps still remain. The Appalachian Trail history site says only the footings remain. Neither gives a date for its description, so the story reports both.

notes_for_editor: Build year is unresolved: 1917 (Trail history site), 1930 (register), with a 1932 newspaper item announcing construction. The 1930 build year on the brief's record is kept only as the register's claim, not as a verified date. The removal year is only 'early 2000s' in the register; the 2000 in events is the start of that range. The 40-foot, 14 x 14 cabin design is from the 1932 announcement and is not confirmed as built. No height_m is recorded for that reason. The 1932 item places the tower on the county line between Amherst and Rockbridge counties; the register says Rockbridge County, and the story uses the register's county. The July 1969 photo is a caption only; no image URL was found, so no photos entry. Lexington and the Trail history site are undated. No staffing or fire records found. Next checks if wanted: Virginia Department of Forestry records, The News Leader microfilm for 1930-1933, and the source of the July 1969 photo.
